title: Dictionary Variables - Key-Value Pairs
description: Store structured data using dictionary variables with &{...} syntax.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Lists are ordered, but sometimes you need named data—like system statuses with component names as keys. That's where dictionaries come in."
story.context: Dictionaries map keys to values. Unlike lists (indexed by number), dictionaries use meaningful names. 'Navigation' → 'OPERATIONAL', 'Power' → 'DEGRADED'. This structure is perfect for configuration, status reports, and structured data.

theory.title: Dictionary Variables: Key-Value Data Structures
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 displays a status board with system names and their conditions.

"PROTO-7, lists are great for ordered data. But when you need named data—where each value has a meaningful key—you need a dictionary."

What is a Dictionary?

A dictionary is a collection of key-value pairs. Think of it like a real dictionary:

  • Key: The word you look up (e.g., "Navigation")
  • Value: The definition/data (e.g., "OPERATIONAL")

In Robot Framework, dictionary variables use the &{dict_name} syntax.

Lists vs Dictionaries

FeatureListDictionary
Access by Index (number) Key (name)
Syntax @{list} &{dict}
Order Always ordered Insertion order (Python 3.6+)
Use case Sequences, iterations Structured data, configs
Example @{fruits} [Apple, Banana] &{status} {nav: OK, power: FAIL}

Creating Dictionaries: The Create Dictionary Keyword

*** Test Cases ***
Basic Dictionary
    &{user}    Create Dictionary    name=Alice    email=alice@example.com    role=Admin
    Log Dictionary    ${user}

Output:

Dictionary size is 3 and it contains following items:
name: Alice
email: alice@example.com
role: Admin

Dictionary Syntax Rules

  • Creation: &{dict} Create Dictionary key1=value1 key2=value2
  • Key-value separator: Use = with NO spaces around it
  • Multiple pairs: Separate with spaces (4 recommended)
  • Keys: Usually strings, but can be numbers
  • Values: Any data type (strings, numbers, lists, even other dicts)

& vs $ with Dictionaries

*** Test Cases ***
Dict Expansion
    &{config}    Create Dictionary    host=localhost    port=8080    ssl=True
    
    # Using &{config} - expands to key=value pairs
    Log Many    &{config}
    # Output: host=localhost, port=8080, ssl=True
    
    # Using ${config} - treats dict as single object
    Log    ${config}
    # Output: {'host': 'localhost', 'port': 8080, 'ssl': True}

Key difference:

  • &{dict}: Expands to key=value pairs (for passing to keywords)
  • ${dict}: Treats the whole dict as one variable

The Log Dictionary Keyword

Log Dictionary is designed for dictionaries:

*** Test Cases ***
Log Dictionary Demo
    &{system}    Create Dictionary    cpu=45%    memory=8GB    disk=512GB    status=healthy
    Log Dictionary    ${system}

Output:

Dictionary size is 4 and it contains following items:
cpu: 45%
memory: 8GB
disk: 512GB
status: healthy

Note: Use ${dict} with Log Dictionary (not &{dict}).

Empty and Single-Entry Dictionaries

*** Test Cases ***
Edge Cases
    # Empty dictionary
    &{empty}     Create Dictionary
    Log Dictionary    ${empty}    # Logs "Dictionary size is 0"
    
    # Single entry
    &{single}    Create Dictionary    status=OK
    Log Dictionary    ${single}   # Logs one key-value pair

Dictionaries in the *** Variables *** Section

You can define dictionaries at the file level:

*** Variables ***
&{API_CONFIG}      base_url=https://api.example.com    timeout=30s    retry=3
&{TEST_USER}       username=testuser@example.com    password=Test123    role=standard

*** Test Cases ***
Use Predefined Dicts
    Log Dictionary    ${API_CONFIG}
    Log Dictionary    ${TEST_USER}

Keys with Spaces (Requires Quotes in Some Contexts)

*** Test Cases ***
Keys With Spaces
    &{data}    Create Dictionary    first name=John    last name=Doe    zip code=12345
    Log Dictionary    ${data}
    # Keys: 'first name', 'last name', 'zip code'

Keys with spaces work but require careful handling when accessing (we'll cover access next exercise).

Real-World Example: System Configuration

*** Test Cases ***
API Health Check
    &{health_status}    Create Dictionary
    ...    database=connected
    ...    cache=connected
    ...    api_server=running
    ...    queue_size=127
    ...    response_time=45ms
    
    Log Dictionary    ${health_status}
    
    # Use the ... continuation for long lines
    # Each ...  line adds more key=value pairs

Note: The ... syntax continues the previous line. Useful for long dictionary definitions!

Nested Structures (Preview)

Dictionary values can be lists or other dictionaries:

*** Test Cases ***
Nested Data
    @{admins}      Create List    alice@example.com    bob@example.com
    &{app_config}  Create Dictionary    admins=${admins}    version=2.1.0
    
    Log Dictionary    ${app_config}
    # Output shows admins: ['alice@example.com', 'bob@example.com']

Common Mistakes

  • ❌ Using key = value (spaces around =): Should be key=value
  • ❌ Using ${dict} instead of &{dict} when creating
  • ❌ Duplicate keys: name=Alice name=Bob → only Bob survives
  • ❌ Using commas: name=Alice, age=30 → comma becomes part of value

MENTOR-9: "Create two dictionaries: one for ship system statuses, another for crew information. Use Log Dictionary to display them. Show me you can structure complex data."
